bleeding_start.text: Is the blood spurting, pumping, or pouring heavily and rapidly?

b_tourniquet_q.text: Is the severe bleeding on an arm or a leg?

b_apply_t.text:
STEP 1:  Place a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the bleeding site (never directly on a joint).
 STEP 2: Tighten it extremely hard until the bleeding completely stops. This will cause the patient severe pain.
 STEP 3: Write the exact time it was applied on the patient's forehead or on the tourniquet. DO NOT remove it.

b_pack_wound.text:
STEP 1: Take clean gauze or clothing and pack it DEEPLY into the wound. 
STEP 2: Press down with both hands using your full body weight.
 STEP 3: Keep continuous pressure. Do not lift to check the wound.

b_direct_pressure.text: Can you apply firm, direct pressure over the wound with a clean cloth?

b_elevate_q.text: Have you held continuous, hard pressure for 5 full minutes without peeking?

b_clean_wrap.text:
The bleeding is controlled.
 Gently rinse the area with clean water.
 Wrap it firmly with a bandage, but ensure you can still slide one finger under the wrap so circulation isn't cut off.

b_pressure_harder.text:
Have the person lie flat to prevent shock.
 DO NOT remove the blood-soaked cloth.
 Add more layers on top, lock your elbows, and press down harder with your body weight. Call 112.

b_find_cloth.text: Quickly grab a clean shirt, towel, or gauze. Place it directly over the cut and press down as hard as you can.

choking_start.text: Is the person able to cough forcefully, cry, or speak?

c_encourage.text: Do not interfere yet. Encourage them to keep coughing forcefully to clear the airway themselves. Monitor closely.

c_conscious_q.text: Is the person still conscious (awake but unable to breathe)?

c_back_blows.text: Stand behind them. Support their chest with one hand and lean them forward. Give 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Did it dislodge?

c_abdominal.text:
STEP 1:  Wrap arms around their waist. Make a fist and place the thumb-side just above their belly button.
 STEP 2: Grasp your fist with the other hand.
 STEP 3: Give 5 quick, hard, upward thrusts (like trying to lift them). Did it work?

c_unconscious_cpr.text:
They have lost consciousness.
 Gently lower them flat on their back to the floor.
 Call 112 immediately.
 Begin CPR starting with chest compressions.
 If you see the object in their mouth, sweep it out, but NEVER do a blind finger sweep.

c_recovery.text:
The airway is clear.
 Sit them down, keep them calm, and ensure they are breathing normally.
 Seek medical evaluation.

unconscious_start.text: Tap their shoulders firmly and shout loudly, 'Are you okay?!'. Do they respond or move?

u_monitor.text: Stay with them. Ask them what happened, loosen tight clothing, and look for any hidden bleeding or medical alert bracelets.

u_breathing_q.text: Tilt their head back slightly. Look at their chest for 10 seconds. Is the chest rising and falling normally (not just occasional gasps)?

u_recovery_pos.text: Did they fall from a height, get hit by a car, or do you suspect a neck/spine injury?

u_roll_side.text:
STEP 1: [Image of first aid recovery position steps]
Kneel beside them. Straighten their legs.
 STEP 2: Bring their far arm across their chest and their far knee up. STEP 3:
 Pull the knee to roll them gently onto their side toward you.
 STEP 4: Tilt their head back to keep the airway open. Wait for 112.

u_leave_flat.text: DO NOT move them. Keep their head absolutely still to protect the spinal cord. Wait for paramedics.

u_start_cpr.text: Call 112. Kneel beside them. Place the heel of one hand in the dead center of their chest, other hand on top, fingers interlocked. Can you push hard and fast?

u_cpr_details.text:
PERFORM CPR: Keep your elbows straight. Push DOWN at least 2 inches deep. Push FAST at a rate of 100 to 120 beats per minute (to the rhythm of the song 'Stayin' Alive'). Let the chest recoil completely between pushes.
 Do not stop until help arrives or they wake up.

u_cpr_encourage.text: You are their only chance. Any CPR is better than no CPR. Lock your elbows, put your weight over their chest, and push hard in the center. Don't worry about hurting them; you need to pump their heart. Keep going!

chest_pain_start.text: Is the chest pain crushing, or spreading to the left arm, back, neck, or jaw?

cp_breathing_q.text: Are they sweating heavily, feeling dizzy, or struggling to catch their breath?

cp_rest.text: Have them rest quietly in a comfortable chair. If the pain does not go away after 5 minutes, call 112 immediately.

cp_sit_down.text: Call 112. Sit them on the floor with their knees bent and head/shoulders supported (the 'W' position) to ease heart strain. Are they allergic to aspirin or bleeding internally?

cp_aspirin.text: Do they have prescribed angina medication, like Nitroglycerin spray or pills?

cp_chew_aspirin.text: Give them 1 adult aspirin (300-325mg) or 4 baby aspirins. Tell them to CHEW the aspirin slowly, do not just swallow it whole. Keep them perfectly still.

cp_nitro.text: Help them self-administer their prescribed Nitroglycerin. Reassure them and keep them calm while waiting for the ambulance.

cp_wait.text: Do NOT give them aspirin. Keep them in the 'W' sitting position, loosen any tight clothing around their neck and waist, and monitor their breathing.

burns_start.text: Is the burn caused by dangerous chemicals or a high-voltage electrical source?

bu_chem_elec.text: CHEMICAL: Brush off dry powder safely, then flush the area with running water for 20 mins. ELECTRICAL: DO NOT touch the person if they are still connected to the power source! Turn off the main breaker first. Call 112.

bu_size_q.text: Is the burn larger than the size of the victim's hand, or located on the face, neck, or groin?

bu_major.text: Call 112. Carefully remove rings, watches, or tight clothing near the burn BEFORE swelling starts. Cover the burn lightly with a clean, dry, lint-free cloth or plastic wrap. DO NOT apply ice, butter, or ointments.

bu_minor.text: Is the skin severely blistered, charred, or broken?

bu_cool_water.text: Place the burn under cool (NOT ice cold) running water for 10 to 20 minutes to stop the burning process in the deep skin layers. Apply aloe vera gel once completely cooled.

bu_blister.text: Cool the burn with running water for 20 minutes. DO NOT pop the blisters—this causes infection. Pat dry gently and cover loosely with a sterile, non-stick gauze pad.

trauma_start.text: Was it a high-speed car crash, a fall from a height, or a heavy blow to the head/back?

t_spine_q.text: Is the person complaining of numbness, tingling in fingers/toes, or severe neck/back pain?

t_immobilize.text: Assume a spinal injury. DO NOT MOVE THEM unless they are in a burning vehicle or immediate mortal danger. Kneel behind their head, place your hands on both sides of their head, and hold it perfectly still until paramedics arrive.

t_open_wound_q.text: Is there a bone protruding through the skin (compound fracture)?

t_stop_bleed.text: Call 112. Place clean padding AROUND the exposed bone to control bleeding. DO NOT push the bone back in. DO NOT apply direct pressure over the bone itself.

t_deformity_q.text: Does the limb look deformed, bent at an unnatural angle, or is it heavily swollen?

t_splint.text: It is likely broken. Do not try to straighten it. Immobilize the limb in the EXACT position you found it. Support it with cushions, rolled clothing, or a makeshift splint tied above and below the joint.

t_rice.text: Follow the R.I.C.E method: REST the injured part. ICE it for 20 minutes wrapped in a cloth. COMPRESS it lightly with an elastic bandage. ELEVATE the limb above heart level to reduce swelling.

allergic_reaction_start.text: Is the person experiencing difficulty breathing, severe swelling of face/lips, or loss of consciousness?

ar_critical.text:
🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY - CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY!

Severe Allergic Reaction (ANAPHYLAXIS) detected. If available, use an EpiPen immediately by injecting into the outer thigh through clothing if necessary. Person needs emergency medical attention NOW. Lay them flat with legs elevated unless vomiting. Monitor breathing constantly.

ar_symptoms_q.text: Has the person ingested something new (food, medication) or been exposed to a known allergen?

ar_known_allergen.text: Is there itching, hives/rash, or mild swelling?

ar_mild_reaction.text:
Mild allergic reaction detected.
 STEP 1: Remove the allergen source immediately.
 STEP 2: Give antihistamine (like diphenhydramine/Benadryl) if available and person is conscious.
 STEP 3: Monitor closely. If symptoms worsen or breathing becomes difficult, call 112.

ar_unknown_trigger.text: Is there any rash, itching, or mild swelling appearing on the skin?

ar_monitor.text: Continue monitoring the patient closely. Watch for signs of allergic reaction: difficulty breathing, swelling, rash, or dizziness. If symptoms develop, seek immediate medical attention. Call 112 if condition worsens.

breathing_difficulty_start.text: Is the person gasping for air, turning blue in the lips/face, or unable to speak in full sentences?

bd_critical.text:
🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY - CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY!

Severe breathing difficulty detected. This is a life-threatening emergency. Sit person upright in a comfortable position. Loosen any tight clothing. Ensure airway is clear. Reassure the patient to remain calm. If person loses consciousness, begin CPR.

bd_partial_q.text: Has the person recently experienced chest pain, wheezing, or previous asthma/respiratory condition?

bd_respiratory_history.text: Do they have a rescue inhaler available (for asthma)?

bd_inhaler_available.text: Help the person use their rescue inhaler immediately. Have them take slow, deep breaths. Sit upright to ease breathing. Wait 5-10 minutes. If breathing does not improve, call 112.

bd_position_comfort.text: Have the person sit upright in a comfortable position. Loosen all tight clothing. Ensure good air circulation. Keep them calm and reassured. Monitor breathing closely. Call 112 if difficulty continues or worsens.

bd_onset_q.text: Did the breathing difficulty start suddenly after exposure to allergen, extreme emotion, or physical exertion?

bd_trigger_manage.text: Remove or eliminate the trigger if possible. Have the person sit in a calm, cool environment. Take slow, deep breaths together (breathing exercises). If breathing doesn't improve in 5 minutes, call 112.

seizure_start.text: Is the person currently shaking/convulsing, unresponsive, or has loss of consciousness?

s_during_seizure.text:
🚨 ACTIVE SEIZURE - DO NOT RESTRAIN THE PERSON!

STEP 1: Clear the area of dangerous objects.
 STEP 2: Place something soft under their head.
 STEP 3: Turn them on their side if possible to keep airway clear.
 STEP 4: DO NOT put anything in their mouth.
 STEP 5: Time the seizure duration.
 STEP 6: Call 112 if seizure lasts more than 5 minutes or if person doesn't regain consciousness.

s_post_seizure_q.text: Has the person already had a seizure and is now recovering/confused?

s_after_seizure.text: Is this the first seizure they've experienced, or do they have a known seizure disorder?

s_first_seizure.text:
First seizure detected - CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY for medical evaluation.
 
While waiting: Keep person in recovery position on their side. Do not leave them alone. Monitor breathing and consciousness. Be prepared to provide CPR if needed. Once conscious, reassure them and explain what happened.

s_known_condition.text: Do they have seizure medications they should take now?

s_medication_available.text: Help them take their seizure medication as prescribed. Place them in recovery position on their side. Monitor closely during recovery. Alert 112 if another seizure occurs.

s_monitor_recovery.text: Person is recovering from seizure. Keep them in safe recovery position on their side. Do not leave alone. Stay calm and reassuring. Monitor for confusion and memory loss. Alert medical services if they have repeated seizures.

s_warning_signs.text: Is the person showing warning signs like numbness, unusual sensations, or strange behavior before a seizure?

s_aura_detected.text:
Warning signs of an upcoming seizure detected (aura). STEP 1: Move person to a safe location away from hazards.
 STEP 2: Place them in recovery position.
 STEP 3: If they have seizure medication, administer it as prescribed. STEP 4: Call 112 and stay with them.

s_other_symptoms.text: Monitor the person closely. If they show any signs of losing consciousness or convulsions, implement seizure protocol and call 112.

stroke_start.text: Is the person's FACE drooping on one side when they try to smile?

stroke_arms_q.text: Can they raise both ARMS equally? Does one arm drift downward?

stroke_arms_problem.text:
⚠️ POSSIBLE STROKE! PERFORM FULL F.A.S.T. CHECK.

F = FACE drooping (already confirmed)
A = ARM weakness (confirmed)
S = SPEECH difficulty (check now)
T = TIME - Call 112 immediately! Time is critical for stroke treatment.

stroke_speech_q.text: Can the person speak clearly? Are words slurred or do they have difficulty finding words?

stroke_speech_problem.text:
🚨 STROKE ALERT - THIS IS A MEDICAL EMERGENCY - CALL 112 NOW!

Note the EXACT time symptoms started (critical for treatment).
Do NOT give food or water in case they cannot swallow safely.
Keep person calm and reassured.
Monitor for additional symptoms.
Stroke treatment must begin within hours for best outcomes.

stroke_other_signs.text: Is the person experiencing sudden: severe headache, dizziness, vision problems, or difficulty walking?

stroke_other_positive.text:
⚠️ POSSIBLE STROKE SYMPTOMS DETECTED - CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY!

Note the EXACT time symptoms started. Person needs urgent medical imaging and evaluation. Do NOT give food/water. Monitor closely. Even if symptoms seem to improve, seek immediate medical attention.

stroke_monitor.text:
Continue monitoring the person closely for any of these stroke signs:
- Facial drooping
- Arm weakness
- Speech difficulty
- Sudden severe headache
- Vision changes
- Dizziness or loss of balance

If ANY of these appear, call 112 immediately.
